steps.title: Import Vue and required APIs (ref, onMounted)
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref, and onMounted from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary functions from Vue's Composition API.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple functions from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

successCriteria: Vue, ref, and onMounted are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the necessary Vue Composition API functions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some items, but make sure to import Vue, ref, and onMounted from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import Vue, ref, and onMounted from 'vue'.

steps.hint: Use the <script setup> syntax to define a Vue component. The template should contain a single root <div> element.
steps.analogousExample: // Example Vue component with script setup
steps.seedCode:
<script setup>
// Import Vue, ref, and onMounted from 'vue'
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Create a root <div> element here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'InfiniteScrollDemo' is created with a template containing a root <div> element.
successCriteria: The component uses <script setup> syntax and has a template with a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the <script setup> section and a template with a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you're using <script setup> and have a template with a root <div> element.

steps.title: Initialize state for items and loading
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, create two reactive variables using ref: one named 'items' initialized as an empty array, and another named 'loading' initialized as false.
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create reactive state. For example: const count = ref(0).
steps.seedCode:
<script setup>
// Import Vue, ref, and onMounted from 'vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create reactive state variables here
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Create a root <div> element here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have two reactive variables ready to store your list items and track loading status.
successCriteria: Two ref variables are created: 'items' (array) and 'loading' (boolean).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the reactive state variables needed for infinite scroll.
steps.feedbackPartial: You created one of the variables, but both 'items' and 'loading' are required.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating two reactive variables using ref: 'items' as an empty array and 'loading' as false.

steps.title: Create a function to fetch more items
steps.instruction: Create an async function named 'loadMoreItems' inside your component's script setup section.
steps.hint: Define an async function that will later handle fetching and adding new items to your reactive state.
steps.seedCode:
<script setup>
// Import Vue, ref, and onMounted from 'vue'
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create reactive state variables here

// Create an async function to load more items
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Create a root <div> element here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an empty async function defined that can be called to load more items.
successCriteria: An async function named 'loadMoreItems' is defined in the script setup section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the loadMoreItems function. Next we'll implement the data fetching logic inside it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is async and named exactly 'loadMoreItems'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should be async and named 'loadMoreItems'. Check the function declaration syntax.

steps.title: Add onMounted lifecycle hook
steps.instruction: Import the onMounted lifecycle hook from 'vue' and use it to call your fetch function when the component loads.
steps.hint: Import onMounted alongside ref, then call onMounted with your fetch function as the callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically call loadMoreItems when it first mounts, loading initial items.
successCriteria: onMounted is imported from 'vue' and used with loadMoreItems as its callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the onMounted lifecycle hook to load items when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported onMounted and called it with loadMoreItems inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported onMounted and used it to call loadMoreItems when the component loads.

steps.title: Create the main container template
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a CSS class to the root <div> element for styling.
steps.hint: Use the class attribute to assign a CSS class name to the div.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a CSS class to a div
steps.expectedOutcome: The root div element will have a CSS class attribute applied.
successCriteria: The root <div> element includes a class attribute with a valid CSS class name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a CSS class to the main container, which will allow you to style it later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a class attribute to the div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The root div element should have a class attribute. Try adding something like class="container" to the div.

steps.title: Display the list of items
steps.instruction: Inside the template's root div, add a <ul> element that uses v-for to render each item in the items array as an <li>.
steps.hint: Use v-for to iterate over items.value and display each item's content.
steps.analogousExample: • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A bulleted list of items appears in the UI when items are loaded.
successCriteria: The template contains a <ul> with v-for that renders each item from items.value as an <li>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the list of items using v-for.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using v-for correctly and rendering each item as an <li> inside a <ul>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list is not displaying correctly. Check that you've added a <ul> with v-for and each item is rendered as an <li>.

steps.title: Add loading indicator
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside your template that shows 'Loading more items...' only when the loading state is true, using Vue's v-if directive.
steps.hint:
Use v-if="loading" on a

element to conditionally render the loading message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a loading indicator that appears only when loading is true.
successCriteria:
A

element with v-if="loading" and the text 'Loading more items...' is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the loading state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a loading indicator, but check the condition or text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading indicator isn't implemented correctly. Review how to use v-if with the loading state.

steps.title: Create scroll detection handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named checkScroll that determines if the user has scrolled to the bottom of the page.
steps.hint: The function should compare the scroll position to the total scrollable height of the document.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named checkScroll is defined that returns true when the user has scrolled near the bottom of the page.
successCriteria: The checkScroll function is created and returns a boolean based on scroll position.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the scroll detection handler. This function will be used to trigger loading more items when the user reaches the bottom.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it properly calculates the scroll position and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll detection handler isn't properly defined. Create a function named checkScroll that checks if the user has scrolled to the bottom.

steps.title: Wire scroll handler to window scroll event
steps.instruction: Add an event listener for the 'scroll' event on the window object that calls your scroll detection handler, and also add the cleanup to remove it when the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Use window.addEventListener('scroll', handler) inside onMounted, and window.removeEventListener('scroll', handler) in onUnmounted.
steps.expectedOutcome: The scroll handler will be triggered when the user scrolls, and the event listener will be properly cleaned up when the component is destroyed.
successCriteria: The window scroll event listener is added in onMounted, calls the scroll detection handler, and is removed in onUnmounted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the scroll handler to the window scroll event, and the cleanup ensures no memory leaks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to both add the event listener in onMounted and remove it in onUnmounted.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll handler isn't properly connected to the window scroll event. Check that you're using window.addEventListener and window.removeEventListener correctly.
